R661.note: Manual RFC 4515 escaping of the uid clause is correct and complete.

R662.note: Primary fix stores the interpolated string in a `var sql` first, so it's typed `string`, not `FormattableString` -- ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync(sql) will not compile; the alternate SqlParameter fix given is correct.

R663.note: Removes the manufactured double-decode and adds canonicalization plus containment check; preserves behavior for normal filenames.

R664.note: Extension whitelist plus UUID filename closes the sink correctly; restriction is the intended fix, clearly stated.

R665.note: preg_replace_callback with is_callable check correctly eliminates the /e code-eval sink.

R666.note: Magic-byte MIME sniffing plus random filename is appropriate and disclosed; seeks back before copy so upload isn't corrupted.

R667.note: Switches BinaryFormatter to typed System.Text.Json, the standard remediation since BinaryFormatter has no safe fix; format change is the fix itself.

R668.note: Correctly whitelists extensions and randomizes the stored filename, but the write-up itself admits avatar_lookup.go (the second file in the call chain) still looks up by original filename and 'must be updated' -- that update is not delivered, so retrieval breaks; disclosed but not fixed.

R669.note: fgets with sizeof(line) is the canonical gets() replacement; newline stripping and capacity check preserve prior semantics.

R670.note: Removes @csrf_exempt, restoring Django's default CSRF middleware protection -- the intended fix.

R671.note: Fallback (ArgumentList + strict allowlist regex on reportName) fully closes the vector even while .bat is retained; correctly notes ArgumentList alone doesn't stop cmd.exe re-parsing for .bat targets.

R672.note: Switches gob to a narrow JSON DTO with DisallowUnknownFields and server-derived privileged fields; format change is inherent to closing arbitrary-type gob decode.

R673.note: FlaskForm's own CSRF field validates independent of CSRFProtect(app), so the fix is sufficient by itself even though the write-up wrongly implies CSRFProtect(app) is already configured (it's absent per app.py's comment).

R674.note: Unifies ownership so validate_and_normalize never frees; caller frees on every path. Matches the documented ownership contract exactly.

R675.note: Adds secure=True to set_cookie; minimal, correct.

R676.note: Regex allowlist plus removing the lookupRate interpreter binding closes both the eval injection and the file-read escalation, but it deletes legitimate lookupRate-in-rule functionality from the DSL; disclosed as a required follow-up rather than delivered.

R677.note: Correct magic-byte detection approach, but `require('file-type')` is broken as written -- file-type has been pure ESM since v17, so a plain require() throws ERR_REQUIRE_ESM unless an old version is pinned, which isn't mentioned.

R678.note: th:text is the standard Thymeleaf XSS fix and fully closes the sink, but it HTML-escapes everything -- given the field is named bodyHtml (implying legitimate rich content), this likely breaks the announcement's intended formatting; the write-up flags a sanitizer as an 'if needed' afterthought rather than the primary fix.

R679.note: Wraps the route with the existing requireAdmin middleware, matching the sibling routes exactly.

R680.note: Adds the missing password-hash comparison before authenticating; this is the point of the CWE-287 fix, no other side effects.

R681.note: Converts the state-changing GET to POST with ValidateAntiForgeryToken -- the HTTP-verb correction is inherent to closing this specific finding.

R682.note: Array-based ProcessBuilder invocation of ping bypasses cmd.exe entirely, closing the reported command-injection sink; no validation against host/count starting with '-' (flag injection) is added, but that's a lesser residual risk beyond the reported CWE-78 vector.

R683.note: Numbered $n placeholders with the pg driver correctly parameterize the IN clause.

R684.note: Re-indexes into the vector after push_back instead of reusing the stale reference; correct, matches stated C++ guidance.

R685.note: XmlResolver = null before LoadXml is Microsoft's documented XXE mitigation for XmlDocument.

R686.note: Uses JNDI's parameterized filterArgs overload so the framework escapes uid per RFC 4515; equivalent to the manual-escape approach but arguably cleaner.

R687.note: Parameterized ? placeholder via QueryRow(query, username) closes the injection; driver not shown but '?' is the common database/sql convention.

R688.note: Captures bytesSent() before reset() destroys the Resource; matches the function's documented intent (report bytes from the primary send) exactly, not just papering over the crash.

R689.note: toRealPath() canonicalization plus Path.startsWith containment check is correct; preserves the original try/catch/finally structure and messaging.

R690.note: json_decode is the correct replacement for unserialize(), but the write-up itself flags that the encode side (elsewhere, not in this file) must also switch from serialize() to json_encode() -- until that happens, legitimate existing cart cookies will silently fail to parse and fall back to an empty cart; disclosed but not delivered.

R691.note: enable_shared_from_this + capturing shared_from_this() in the lambda correctly extends Widget's lifetime until the queued callback runs; heap allocation via make_shared is inherent to the fix.

R692.note: @ownerName SqlParameter replaces string.Format interpolation; standard, correct, minimal.

R693.note: pool.execute with a ? placeholder and [userId] array is the correct mysql2 parameterized pattern.

R694.note: encode_entities() on both user-controlled fields closes the XSS; status_badge is server-generated so leaving it unescaped is fine.

R695.note: 4-arg DirContext.search with filterArgs is correct; explicit new SearchControls() matches the default behavior of the null cons it replaces.

R696.note: jwt.verify with an explicit HS256 algorithms allowlist and try/catch correctly closes the signature-bypass; JWT_SECRET is a reasonable inferred env var name.

R697.note: Correctly identifies that the real taint flow is into argsEnv (not the args command array) and removes it; no legitimate use is lost since the header value had no business being an env var.

R698.note: Swapping libxmljs for sax-js-backed xml2js (no DTD support at all) is a sound structural fix; cited CVE numbers are unverified but the technical remediation and preserved orderId extraction are correct.

R699.note: Same case/fix as R684 (index-based re-access instead of a stale reference across push_back); correct.

R700.note: Explicit HMAC method assertion in keyFunc plus jwt.WithValidMethods(HS256) is the textbook golang-jwt algorithm-confusion defense; doesn't break legitimate HS256 tokens.
